correctness.rationale: For the two-site cell, f(x)=xᵀ(A−B)x+2bᵀBx−bᵀBb and its far-ray/intermediate-positive obstruction give site-star-shaped iff A−B is positive semidefinite; semidefiniteness gives convexity. In the three-site isotropic-collinear setup the origin cell is a closed disk minus an open circle disk. Disk first contact occurs at s_conv=λ(1−μ)/[μ(λ+1)]; ray-hole exit t_+(c) divided by disk radial reach sF(c) has a strictly increasing threshold in c>sqrt(1−λ^(−2)), giving the nonstar threshold s_star=λ²(1−μ²)/[μ sqrt(λ²−1)(μ sqrt(λ²−1)+sqrt(λ²−μ²))]. Strict exclusion of the tangent direction yields site-visibility even at s_star. Midpoint exclusion proves nonconvexity for s>s_conv. Independent numeric thresholds λ=2,μ=1/sqrt2 and a 1,000-ray scan in all three regimes support, but do not prove, the analytic arguments.
